meta.title: Product Documentation
meta.subtitle: A concise guide for building, validating, testing, and operating agentic workflows.

steps.title: Create or import
steps.body: Start from a blank flow, paste a flow JSON, or import a JSON file. Imported flows are checked for schema validity and output-name collisions.

steps.title: Add nodes
steps.body: Drag nodes from the library, connect them on the canvas, and configure each node from its details modal.

steps.title: Validate outputs
steps.body: Every output variable should be unique. Use the collision warning modal to rename outputs or intentionally ignore warnings.

steps.title: Save and deploy
steps.body: Save the full flow JSON. Unsaved changes are tracked for canvas changes and node modal edits.

sections.label: Flow Studio
sections.summary: Create and maintain visual agent workflows.
sections.description: Flow Studio is the main workspace for creating flows, arranging nodes, managing edges, editing flow details, cloning, importing, and bulk-managing workflows.
features: Blank, paste, and file-import creation modes
Modern canvas with selectable nodes and subtle colored focus states
Unsaved-change guard before leaving a flow
Multi-select delete across paginated flow lists
JSON spec view for advanced users
howTo: Review validation warnings, then create the flow.
Open the flow and configure nodes.

dataShape.name: Customer Support Flow
dataShape.description: Routes customer questions to the correct tool or agent.

tips: Use clear flow names; they appear in listings and the studio header.
Keep graphSpec.description empty. Flow description belongs at the root level.
Use import preview to confirm node names before creating from JSON.

sections.label: ReAct Agent
sections.summary: Configure autonomous agents with prompts, memory, tools, and outputs.
sections.description: The ReAct Agent node follows a reasoning/action pattern. It can use configured tools, maintain memory, and return a final response into a named output variable.
features: Dedicated tabs: Configuration, Prompt, Memory, Tools, Output, Info
Tool picker for registered tools and MCP tools
Dynamic parameters for model-filled tool arguments
Config mapping from selected tool input parameters
Output variable mapping for downstream nodes
howTo: Open the ReAct Agent node details.
Set the model and runtime values in Configuration.
Write the system instructions in Prompt.
Add tools from the Tools tab and map config values.
Set the final output variable in Output.
tips: Tool name is what the LLM sees; node_type is the executable registered node type.
Use placeholders like {{product_id}} in config when a dynamic parameter should fill the value.
Keep prompts specific and include clear tool usage rules.

sections.label: Validation
sections.summary: Catch output collisions and unsafe flow structure before save or import.
sections.description: Validation focuses on output variable collisions and invalid flow JSON. Users can rename outputs or intentionally skip known-safe warnings.
features: Collision detection across all node output variables
Open the correct node and Output tab from warning actions
Ignore one warning or skip all current warnings
Flow JSON validity checks during Paste and Import
howTo: Review collision warnings when they appear.
Click Rename in node to open the node Output tab.
Use Ignore only this warning only when the collision is intentional.
tips: Prefer unique output variable names for every node.
Skipping validation should be rare and intentional.
Imported flows should be validated before creation.

sections.label: Tools & MCP
sections.summary: Register reusable capabilities and attach them to ReAct agents.
sections.description: Tools and MCP servers are callable capabilities. ReAct agents select from these capabilities during execution based on the tool name, description, config, and dynamic parameters.
features: Registered tool search
MCP server tool search
Config editor from node input parameters
Dynamic parameter schema for model-filled inputs
Tool schema stored inside ReAct Agent inputParameters
howTo: Search and select a registered capability.
Review config values and add dynamic parameters if needed.
tips: Descriptions decide when the model chooses a tool.
Keep dynamic parameter names aligned with config placeholders.
Use MCP tools for external capability discovery.

sections.label: Dictionary
sections.summary: Manage reusable variables used across flows.
sections.description: The Dictionary stores reusable local and global values that can be referenced by templates such as {{CHAT_QUERY}} or business-specific variables.
features: Global dictionary values
Flow-level dictionary configuration
Variable templates in node inputs
Validation for key and value shape
howTo: Create dictionary variables in the Dictionary page.
Select or create variables needed by the flow.
Reference them using {{variable_name}} in node fields.
tips: Use uppercase names for external input placeholders.
Use clear scopes so builders know where values come from.

sections.label: Admin Registry
sections.summary: Manage registered tools, models, and agents.
sections.description: The Admin Registry provides controlled creation and editing of tools, models, and agents. Version is generated by the UI and still sent to backend payloads.
features: Tools, Models, and Agents registry tables
Input/output parameter editors
Import/export JSON helpers
status=all list queries for complete admin visibility
Backend-safe version defaults
tips: Do not ask users for version; it is handled automatically.
Use status=all for admin list screens.

sections.label: Voice
sections.summary: Configure speech input and output for flows.
sections.description: Voice settings define text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and the interaction mode for a voice-enabled agent flow.
features: TTS provider selection
STT provider selection
Voice/text interaction mode
Flow-level voice configuration payload
howTo: Choose TTS, STT, and interaction mode.
tips: Plain text mode disables voice behavior while preserving config.
